title: Cleaning up AWS resources
idea: Cleanup means deleting every resource you created, in dependency order, so nothing keeps running or billing after the course.
points: Running Fargate tasks and load balancers bill by time; ECR bills by data stored.
The cluster, load balancer, target group, repository and log group are separate resources.
Order matters: a cluster must hold no services, a target group no listener rule.
`--force` deletes a repository's images, and deletes a service without scaling it down.

items.label: Service
items.text: Delete first. It keeps replacing tasks, and a cluster refuses while it exists.

items.label: Cluster
items.text: Needs no services and no active tasks, so it comes second.

items.label: Load balancer
items.text: Delete it; its listeners go with it. It bills for each hour it runs.

items.label: Target group
items.text: Deletable only once no listener rule refers to it.

items.label: ECR repository
items.text: Stored images bill by size. `--force` removes the images too.

items.label: Log group
items.text: Deleting it permanently deletes the logs inside.

code.title: Cleanup
code.caption: Every resource from this chapter, deleted in order. Angle brackets mark placeholders.

walk.text: Delete the service; `--force` skips scaling to zero first. Its tasks stop.
Wait until the service is `INACTIVE`. If the next command reports active tasks, retry shortly.
Delete the cluster. It must hold no services and no active tasks.
Delete the load balancer. Its listeners are deleted with it.
Delete the target group. No listener rule may use it.
Delete the repository; `--force` also deletes every image inside it.
Delete the log group. This permanently deletes the stored logs.

code.title: Check
code.caption: Afterwards, list what is left. Each command reports only the current Region.

walk.text: A deleted cluster may linger for a while as `INACTIVE`.
An empty list means no load balancer remains in this Region.
An empty list means no repository remains in this Region.

pitfalls: Use the same Region you built in; each Region lists only its own resources.
Delete the load balancer before its target group, which a listener may still use.
Check each name and ARN before you run a delete command.

quiz.q: You deleted the cluster. Which resource can still be billing?
options: The Docker image on your laptop
The load balancer, if you left it
quiz.why: The load balancer is its own resource and bills for each hour it runs. Deleting the cluster does not remove it.

takeaway: Delete in dependency order, then list what is left to confirm nothing remains.
